chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Former policeman Jimmy Walters, a rock singer who had never heard Basie
summary: A rock singer and ex-Estes Park policeman sang with Horace for three years; he had never heard of 'Stardust' or Basie.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah, use a stock bridge, old pattern, you know. But, oh, this guy knows a wealth of lyrics and he's excellent. Then I had a young guy when I played at Estes Park, another vocalist that played the fender bass. And He played good guitar -- named Jamie Jimmy Walters. And the funny thing about him, when he first came with the group, he was a rock singer, and he knew all the he only knew about five tunes other than rock; only rock. And before I got him, he was a policeman in Estes Park. And he had a nice voice. And he always loved music, though. I think he got canned from the police department because he always was parked somewhere and had the radio on. You know, (unintelligible) and he had this jazz going.
So it was just a matter of time before he had to pursue another position in life. profession (unintelligible). So I got him to start

singing with me, and he stayed with me three years. He's quite a little singer, and I taught him quite a few tunes. He'd never heard of "Stardust." He'd never heard of Count Basie's band. This is how square he was. I said, "Don't you ever tell anybody that, man, if you intend to do this."
You act like you them, anyway, and he just laughed. know you know, just laughing. He's got a great sense of humor. So that's the story on my current group.
